title: Broad non-compete
pattern: Party agrees not to engage in any competing business anywhere in the world for several years after the agreement ends.
explanation: Wide geographic scope and long duration can block the business from its own market and may be unenforceable.
recommendation: Limit to 6-12 months, a defined region and a narrowly defined competing activity.

title: Unlimited one-sided indemnity
pattern: Party shall indemnify and hold harmless the other party against all claims, losses and damages of any kind without limit.
explanation: Uncapped, one-way indemnity exposes you to unlimited financial liability.
recommendation: Make indemnity mutual, cap it at fees paid, and exclude indirect damages.

title: Liability cap that protects only one side
pattern: Provider's liability is excluded entirely while customer remains fully liable for all damages.
explanation: Asymmetric liability leaves you with all risk and no recourse.
recommendation: Request a mutual liability cap tied to contract value.

title: Automatic renewal with long notice period
pattern: Agreement renews automatically for successive terms unless cancelled in writing at least ninety days before expiry.
explanation: Easy to miss the cancellation window and become locked in for another term.
recommendation: Shorten notice to 30 days or require a reminder before renewal.

title: Termination for convenience by one party only
pattern: Provider may terminate at any time without cause or notice while customer cannot terminate before the term ends.
explanation: One-sided exit rights create dependency and unpredictable service loss.
recommendation: Make termination rights mutual with at least 30 days notice and a pro-rata refund.

title: Perpetual confidentiality
pattern: Confidentiality obligations continue forever and survive termination indefinitely with no exceptions.
explanation: Indefinite secrecy duties are costly to track and can conflict with legal disclosure needs.
recommendation: Limit to 2-5 years and add standard exceptions (public info, legal compulsion).

title: Overbroad IP assignment
pattern: All intellectual property, ideas and work product created by the party, including pre-existing materials, are assigned exclusively to the other party.
explanation: You may lose ownership of your pre-existing tools, code or know-how.
recommendation: Carve out pre-existing IP and assign only deliverables created specifically for the contract.

title: Unfavourable jurisdiction or arbitration
pattern: All disputes must be resolved by binding arbitration in a distant foreign jurisdiction at the expense of the customer.
explanation: Distant venues make disputes costly and discourage enforcing your rights.
recommendation: Negotiate a neutral or local venue and shared arbitration costs.

title: Punitive late-payment charges
pattern: Late payments incur interest of three percent per month plus recovery costs and immediate suspension of services.
explanation: Rates this high can be unreasonable and compound quickly.
recommendation: Cap interest at a reasonable annual rate and add a cure period.

title: Unrestricted data use or sharing
pattern: Provider may use, share or sell customer data and personal data to third parties for any purpose without consent.
explanation: May breach data protection laws (e.g., India's DPDP Act, GDPR) and expose customer data.
recommendation: Restrict data use to service delivery, require a DPA and consent for sharing.
